subject: Request: custom uptime/latency exhibit + order form language for HealthGrid MSA
messages:
From: Susan Lee <susan.lee@healthgrid.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Andrew Miles <andrew.miles@healthgrid.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Requesting custom uptime & latency exhibit for MSA / order form language

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the overview last week. Procurement at HealthGrid has reviewed the MSA and the standard Redwood SLA and we'd like to request a custom exhibit that captures two items before legal will sign:

1) An explicit allowance for a monthly maintenance window (up to 4 hours per month) where best-effort latency guarantees are relaxed, documented as a scheduled "planned maintenance" exception;
2) A clarified latency SLO for our interactive inference endpoints (p95 under 300ms for sequences <= 512) with an associated credit schedule tied to per-minute availability.

Attached is a short packet with our suggested language and our internal procurement checklist (HealthGrid_SLA_Request_20260802.pdf). We also need the exact order form wording to show the finance team how credits and billing adjustments will be applied if the agreed SLOs are missed. Can you loop in Legal and Procurement contacts on your side and share a proposed addendum?

Appreciate it — we are trying to close before the end of August.

Best,
Susan Lee
Director, Procurement | HealthGrid
(susan.lee@healthgrid.com)

Attachments: HealthGrid_SLA_Request_20260802.pdf (2 pages)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Andrew Miles <andrew.miles@healthgrid.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T11:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Requesting custom uptime & latency exhibit for MSA / order form language

Hi Susan — thanks for sending the packet and the timeline.

We're happy to propose an SLA exhibit and corresponding order form language that reflects the two items you called out. For transparency, two quick notes from our side:
- Planned maintenance windows are standard but we normally limit them to non-overlapping, announced windows and keep them to 2 hours/month for the hosted plan. 4 hours/month is doable as an exception for Dedicated/Private customers; we'll need to mark it as a documented exception in the exhibit.
- The p95 300ms latency for seq<=512 is aggressive on shared capacity; we can commit to that on a Dedicated pool with the quantization/instance profile described in the addendum. If you need that on Hosted, we'll propose a fall-back that ties the SLO to a dedicated capacity SKU or a higher-tier SLA.

I attached an initial draft addendum for your review (redwood_sla_addendum_draft_v1.docx) that includes:
- Exhibit A: Availability & Maintenance Exceptions
- Exhibit B: Latency SLOs and measurement method (p95, instrumentation)
- Exhibit C: Credit schedule and order form phrasing (billing offsets per missed SLO)

Can you confirm whether your legal prefers inline redlines or a marked-up Word doc? If it's easier, I can also propose explicit order form line-items for the Dedicated pool SKU and the SLA credit percentages.

Next steps we propose:
1) You review the draft and send redlines by EOD 2026-08-11
2) We iterate and produce a final addendum for signature (DocuSign) by 2026-08-18

Looping in Marissa (our contracts lead) and Ben (solutions) to help with redlines and capacity planning.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood_sla_addendum_draft_v1.docx (editable draft)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: (none)
Date: 2026-08-10T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: quick redlines on HG addendum draft

Neha / Ben — sending quick internal comments before we send back to HealthGrid. I'm pasting short redlines here (will mark up the Word doc next):

- Planned maintenance: change to "up to 4 cumulative hours per calendar month, scheduled with >=72 hours notice, not to exceed 1 contiguous window of 4 hours unless mutually agreed." This prevents splitting windows across regions.
- Measurement: define where p95 is measured (edge vs. application-level). Recommend we measure at the Redwood public API ingress for Hosted and at the customer VPC egress point for Private/Dedicated. Keep explicit measurement for seq<=512 and provide method to audit logs for 30 days.
- Credits: propose a cap of 25% of monthly invoice per occurrence, cumulative cap 75% per month. Also require customer to open a support ticket within 7 days to claim credit.
- Hosted vs Dedicated: call out that the p95 300ms is guaranteed only on Dedicated SKUs; for Hosted, offer an "SLA Premium" option (additional monthly fee) that reserves a fraction of capacity and enables the 300ms SLO.

Ben — can you confirm whether the Dedicated pool described in the draft (2x c5-equivalent per shard, prefix cache enabled) will meet 300ms p95 for seq<=512? If not, list the recommended instance profile and the expected price delta so we can include order form line items.

I'll attach a redlined Word shortly.

Marissa
VP, Customer Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Andrew Miles <andrew.miles@healthgrid.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Requesting custom uptime & latency exhibit for MSA / order form language

Hi Susan — thanks for the patience and for the helpful packet. Per our internal review we've attached an updated addendum that reflects the exceptions and order form language we discussed. Highlights:  

- Planned maintenance: up to 4 cumulative hours/month, scheduled with >=72 hours notice; single contiguous window of up to 4 hours unless mutually agreed.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 300ms for sequences <= 512 when served from Redwood Dedicated pool (SKU: DED-RT-300). For Hosted customers we are offering an SLA Premium add-on (SKU: HST-SLA-PREM) that reserves capacity and supports the same SLO. Measurement point is Redwood API ingress for Hosted and Dedicated egress for Private deployments; logs available for audit for 30 days.
- Credit schedule: per-occurrence credit up to 25% of monthly charges for affected services; cumulative cap 75% for the month. Credits require a support ticket opened within 7 days of the incident.

Attached materials: redwood_sla_addendum_draft_v1.docx (redlined with our edits), hg_evidence_packet.zip (requested telemetry snippets and measurement examples). We also drafted suggested order form language you can paste into your procurement docs:  

Order form snippet (suggested):
- Product: Redwood Dedicated Inference (DED-RT-300)
- Term: 12 months
- SLA Exhibit: Redwood SLA Addendum v1 (attached)
- Price: $XX,XXX/month (see rate card)
- Credits: per SLA exhibit; claims must be submitted via support ticket within 7 days

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether HealthGrid prefers inline redlines or a marked-up Word by 2026-08-23.
2) If confirmed, we'll finalize for signature and send a DocuSign link (target signature by 2026-08-25).

Would you like us to include a short one-page FAQ for Finance that maps missed-SLO scenarios to invoice adjustments? We can provide that as a table.

Thanks — looping Marissa and Ben for any last-minute technical/contract notes.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood_sla_addendum_draft_v1.docx (redlined), hg_evidence_packet.zip (telemetry examples)
